**What would change the assessment:** First unopposed and then opposed NFL work in OTAs and camp; how he holds a gap when the guard and center combine on him.

updates.text: Donald's first step beat Turner on one one-on-one rep. The Brewster-Turner combination moved him from the strong A-gap and he split it once. Pleasant's double-team coaching point was pad level; a pass-rush win does not answer the anchor question.
updates.source: Source: [dated camp observations](career/2014/Training_Camp_and_Preseason/Training_Camp/training_report.md). This coaching update preserves the opening grades above.

short.text: Aaron Donald is a rookie defensive tackle, Jacksonville's first-round pick in 2014, and he has been active for {{2014.regular.games:words}} games in his first NFL season. He is undersized but explosive, with a first step and hand quickness that beat blockers before they set; in camp his first step beat Trai Turner on a one-on-one rep. His anchor against double teams is below a starter's standard and holding his gap on early downs is still unproven at his size; in camp the Mike Brewster and Trai Turner double team moved him off the strong A-gap on almost every recorded rep.

transactions.text: Signed a four-year rookie contract with Jacksonville
